verdict.rationale: Solid documents the performance foundations for growing apps: fine-grained updates that rerun only dependent code, built-in Context and Stores for global state, TypeScript support, and free-form code organization. One user reports a largish product staying intuitive and debuggable over a year. However, nothing first-party addresses large-team or large-codebase maintainability directly, and community reports name real scaling caveats: alpha dev tools, reactivity pitfalls with no lint, ecosystem gaps, and a verdict of 'good for small experienced teams'. missing for 10: first-party guidance on structuring large apps and teams, mature dev tooling, lint safeguards against lost reactivity, broader independent evidence of large-team deployments.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build large applications that stay fast and maintainable as my team and codebase grow

citations.quote: when a piece of state changes, only the code that depends on it will rerun
Performant state management is built-in with Context and Stores: you don't have to reach for a third party library to manage global state
you're free to organize your code how you like and you don't have to learn a new rendering system
Having used Solid on a largish web product for over a year, the user will not return to React.
